name: BoringLocal
tagline: Local SEO tooling for small businesses: Google Business Profile upkeep, local ranking visibility, and the boring recurring work that moves the map pack.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The dashboard part of local SEO is genuinely simple software: a keyword list, a location, a scheduled rank check, a chart, a checklist of things you keep forgetting to do. An agent can wire that up in a weekend and you will own your own history instead of renting it. What you cannot conjure is the data underneath, which means paying a SERP or places API per query and, if you want review and post management, surviving Google Business Profile API approval. And the actual value of a service like this is often the doing, not the seeing: someone posting weekly, chasing reviews, fixing citations. A dashboard that shows you your neglect is not the same as a service that ends it.
coreLoopDIY: Tracks your chosen keywords for one business location on a geo grid, stores the history locally, charts movement over time, and nags you through a recurring local SEO checklist.
requirements: Node 20+ and a machine or cheap VPS that can run a nightly cron
A paid SERP or places API key for rank data, billed per query
Google Business Profile API access and OAuth approval if you want reviews and posts, otherwise CSV import
Your own patience for the recurring tasks the tool only reminds you about
whatYouLose: Rank data you did not pay for: every grid point is a metered API call, and grids get expensive fast
Citation and directory coverage, which is a pile of vendor relationships and manual submissions, not an endpoint
Competitor benchmarking and category-level context that comes from tracking thousands of locations
Someone accountable for actually doing the weekly posting, review replies, and cleanup
Any support when Google quietly changes how the map pack or the API behaves
moatNotes: Local SEO products sit on top of platform APIs they do not control, so the durable part is accumulated ranking history plus the willingness to do repetitive work on a schedule.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the owner of a plumbing company does not want a dashboard, they want the map pack position to go up without thinking about it again. A self-built tracker gives you numbers and a to-do list, and the to-do list stays undone, which is exactly why the paid version exists. Add per-query data costs and the API approval slog and the monthly fee starts looking like a fair trade for not caring.
notes: Build this if you enjoy the work and want your own rank history; buy it if the point was to stop thinking about local SEO.
prompt:
Build a single-user local SEO tracker for one business location that I run myself.

Stack, no alternatives: Next.js App Router with TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite through better-sqlite3, Recharts for graphs. No auth, no accounts, no telemetry, no hosted services. It runs with npm run dev on my machine or a small VPS.

Config lives in config.json at the repo root: business name, address, latitude, longitude, primary category, and a list of tracked keywords. Secrets live in .env: SERP_API_KEY and optionally GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, GOOGLE_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN.

Core loop, in scope:
1. A script scripts/scan.ts that, for each keyword, queries a SERP or places provider at a configurable geo grid around the business coordinates (default 3x3, grid spacing in km configurable) and records the business rank at each point, plus the top three competitors seen.
2. Store every scan in SQLite: scans, scan_points, rankings, competitors. Never overwrite history.
3. A dashboard route showing, per keyword: current average rank, change since last scan, a heat grid of the geo points, and a line chart of average rank over time.
4. A recurring checklist feature: tasks with a cadence (weekly, monthly, quarterly) such as post an update, reply to new reviews, verify hours, check NAP consistency. Show what is overdue on the dashboard. Completions are logged in SQLite.
5. A reviews page: if Google Business Profile credentials are present, fetch reviews and show unanswered ones; if not, support importing a CSV of reviews. Do not pretend the API works without approval, print a clear message instead.
6. A markdown export of the last 90 days: rank movement per keyword, tasks completed, reviews gained.

Out of scope, do not build: multi-tenant anything, billing, user management, automated directory or citation submission, scraping Google HTML directly, AI-generated review replies or blog content.

Before each scan, estimate and print the number of API calls the run will make so I can see the cost. Cache scan results for a configurable minimum interval so I cannot accidentally spend money twice in one day.

Include a seed script with fake ranking history so the charts are populated on first run, a README covering the API key setup and the cron line for a nightly scan, and Vitest tests for the grid generation and rank aggregation math.
